answer: Rewards are computed per operator root, not per key, on a concave curve. The ledger groups identities that provably share a controller and pays that root sublinearly: a thousand keys collect sixty times one key, well under linear payout. Keys are free, so an operator scatters them across a tundra of rented hosts. Each addition dilutes its own marginal return, and the horizon where clones break even recedes faster than the farm can grow; splitting stays dominated by working alone. Track record is the scarce input, opening on its own schedule, like a lotus, never on demand.
